name: Cryptovoxels
rootCause: According to reports, someone pretended to be a Cryptovoxels official to conduct a phishing attack, induced users to authorize, stole multiple NFTs (including Cryptovoxels Parcel Token, Art Blocks: BLOCKS Token, Mutant Ape Yacht Club: MAYC Token, etc.), and then sold them on opensea. It is reported that anonymous attackers used a vulnerability in the Discord bot to manage to direct community users to phishing sites on the official Cryptovoxels Discord channel. The attacker's address is 0x794ca38bc1e15e528a7991ce25707a25ad71b675.

descriptions.text: According to reports, someone pretended to be a Cryptovoxels official to conduct a phishing attack, induced users to authorize, stole multiple NFTs (including Cryptovoxels Parcel Token, Art Blocks: BLOCKS Token, Mutant Ape Yacht Club: MAYC Token, etc.), and then sold them on opensea. It is reported that anonymous attackers used a vulnerability in the Discord bot to manage to direct community users to phishing sites on the official Cryptovoxels Discord channel. The attacker's address is 0x794ca38bc1e15e528a7991ce25707a25ad71b675.

On March 28, 2022, attackers compromised the Cryptovoxels Discord to post phishing links, tricking users into signing malicious transactions and stealing approximately $171,000 worth of assets on Ethereum Mainnet. Losses primarily affected individual user wallets, not the project treasury. A phishing attack exploited a vulnerability in a Discord bot to distribute malicious links, leading users to connect their wallets to a fake site and approve harmful transactions. The exploit targeted user operational security, not smart contract logic.
